Element.attribute:
The Definition of Done is a list of conditions that an item of work must meet before it is deemed complete. Conditions included in the Definition of Done are applicable either to all work items (i.e., entire Product Backlog) or a subset of work items (i.e. individual Backlog Items). In the event there are material differences in the outputs of various work items, be sure to develop conditions  specific to a related subset of work as opposed to using a generic set across all work items (i.e., the entire Product Backlog).

Conditions included in the Definition of Done are typically supplemented by additional criteria specific to an individual component of work (i.e., acceptance criteria for a specific Backlog Item).

All members of the team must have a shared understanding of the conditions to provide transparency and product quality.

Definition of Done typically includes criteria, which oblige the Development Team to:

  • Create agreed documentation
  • Meet non-functional requirements (mainly applies to technical deliveries)
  • Test, as needed (mainly applies to technical deliveries)
  • Store code or documents
  • Obtain peer or Product Owner review
  • Meet defined acceptance criteria

The Definition of Done is not a static list. As the team and stakeholders learn more about the product, as it is created, or the creation process itself, they may update the criteria. It is important that revisions to the Definition of Done are implemented prior to the start of a sprint as the pace of work would be disturbed if introduced during in-flight sprints.
To guide the team their work so that the resulting product meets expected quality criteria and satisfies stakeholder expectations.

• Clearly visible list displayed in the Development Team's working area
  • An electronically shared list such as one maintained in either a(n):
    • electronic team collaboration tool
    • slide
    • spreadsheet
